title: How to choose the spoken language for captions on iPhone
job: In Vyra on iPhone, tap Captions, choose the audio under Generate from and set Spoken language before generating the captions. Choose the language being spoken in the recording.

title: How to remove captions from one section of a video on iPhone
job: In Vyra on iPhone, select the unwanted caption on the timeline and use Delete. Keep the underlying video and audio selected separately so the spoken recording stays in the edit.

title: How to let speech continue over the next shot on iPhone
job: To make an L-cut in Vyra on iPhone, keep the outgoing shot’s speech playing while the picture changes to the next shot. Ask chat to preserve the complete sentence and change only the visible footage at that point.
source: Audio features and Editing tools on iPhone

title: How to lower music only during speech on iPhone
job: In Vyra on iPhone, ask chat to lower the music during the spoken passages and bring it back gradually in the gaps. Keep the voice track unchanged and review every transition by listening.

title: How to slow down one section of a video on iPhone
job: In Vyra on iPhone, identify the exact action and ask chat to slow only that section. Keep the surrounding clips at their original pace and check the sound at both boundaries.

title: How to keep one music track playing across video cuts on iPhone
job: In Vyra on iPhone, add the chosen music once and ask chat to keep it continuous beneath the sequence of clips. Review each picture cut for duplicate music or a jump in the recording.

title: How to make video text appear at the reveal on iPhone
job: In Vyra on iPhone, add the text and ask chat to start it at the moment the result becomes visible. Specify when the text should disappear so it does not cover the setup or the next section.

title: How to find video ideas inside Vyra on iPhone
job: In Vyra for iPhone version 0.1.9, open the Ideas tab to browse short videos picked for your niche, or tap the Vyra button on a main screen to ask for ideas. Choose something you can make with your own footage.

title: Photography video ideas that show how you made the image
job: Show the decision behind one photograph. A change in framing or light gives the viewer something specific to compare.

title: Stop-motion behind-the-scenes video ideas
job: Pair a finished stop-motion moment with the physical change that made it happen. Use your rendered animation as supplied footage and show the setup separately.

title: Language-learning video ideas from your own practice
job: Build a language-learning video around one real practice moment. Let the recorded phrase remain audible and keep any explanation clearly separate from the transcription.

title: Repair video ideas that show the fault and the result
job: A repair video needs a visible fault and a result that can be checked. Film those from comparable angles and keep any limits of the repair in your explanation.

title: Book review video ideas built around your own reading
job: Choose one observation you can explain from your reading. A clear reason to recommend or hesitate helps more than a fast stack of covers.

title: Walking-tour video ideas for one route or place
job: Give a walking video a route the viewer can follow. Use a beginning, a recognizable stop and an ending rather than implying that unrelated locations sit beside each other.

title: Study video ideas with a clear task and stopping point
job: Show the task you started, the point where you checked your understanding and the work you actually finished. A tidy desk alone cannot show what you learned.

title: Dance rehearsal video ideas from takes you already filmed
job: Choose one phrase of movement and let it play long enough to follow. Use the rehearsal recordings to show a decision without presenting an edited sequence as one continuous take.

title: Gardening video ideas from changes you have recorded
job: Use the same view across recorded dates to show a change in the garden. Label the actual interval instead of making a short montage stand in for unrecorded growth.

title: Cooking prep video ideas that keep the useful steps visible
job: Give a cooking-prep video one practical outcome. Keep the step or texture change the viewer needs to see, even when the rest of the preparation is shortened.

title: Board-game video ideas for one turn or decision
job: Explain one decision at the table. Keep the relevant pieces visible and distinguish your personal strategy from the game’s official rules.

title: Skateboarding video ideas from a filmed session
job: Keep the full recorded attempt visible when the landing matters. A sequence can show effort and context without using cuts that make an incomplete attempt look complete.
